seo.title: Landscaping FAQ: Quotes, Permits & Scheduling | RNC
seo.description: Answers on how quotes work, tree permits, watering rules, scheduling and what our maintenance includes across Greater Victoria. Ask us for a free quote.

lede: How quotes work, local rules, scheduling and what to expect.

faqs.a: Every property is different, so we don't publish prices. We quote from a site visit or your photos and a written scope that lists the work, frequency and schedule. The quote is free. [Get a free quote](/free-quote/).
Yes. There is no charge to request or receive a quote.

faqs.q: What affects the price of a quote?
faqs.a: Size of the area, access, the condition of the site, materials, disposal, how often we visit and the season. Your written quote states the assumptions.

faqs.q: How soon will I hear back?
faqs.a: We reply within [REPLY TIME]. If it's urgent, call [PHONE].

faqs.q: What happens after I send a request?
faqs.a: We read it, reply within [REPLY TIME] with any questions, and arrange a site visit if the job needs one. Then you get a written quote with the scope and schedule. See [how we work](/process/).

faqs.q: Can you quote to our specification or tender?
faqs.a: Yes. Describe it in the quote form, then attach it to the email that opens, or send it to [EMAIL]. We'll quote to it. See [commercial](/commercial/).

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to cut down or prune a tree?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Most municipalities here have a tree bylaw, and many protect Garry oak, arbutus and other native species at small sizes. We check before any work. See [tree permits and winter pruning](/resources/winter-pruning-and-storm-prep/). This is general information, not legal advice.

faqs.q: What are the CRD watering days?
faqs.a: From May 1 to September 30, CRD Stage 1 rules allow lawn watering on two days a week, set by your address, in the early morning or evening. Hand watering and drip irrigation of gardens are allowed any day. Our [watering guide](/resources/crd-watering-rules-guide/) has the full schedule and the link to the CRD.

faqs.q: How do you dispose of invasive plants?
faqs.a: We keep them separate from green waste and dispose of them following CRD guidance.

faqs.q: How often should a lawn be mowed?
faqs.a: In spring growth, weekly or every other week is common. Summer and winter need less. Your plan sets the frequency.
Yes. Pruning, cleanups, storm debris and some installation continue through Greater Victoria's mild winters.

faqs.q: Do I need to be home?
faqs.a: No, as long as we can reach the work area safely. Tell us about gates, pets and parking in your request.
Mowing, edging, bed care, pruning and seasonal cleanups, as listed in your scope. See [grounds maintenance](/services/grounds-maintenance/).
It can. We install drip or spray zones during a build, or service an existing system. See [irrigation](/services/irrigation/).
Yes, after checking whether a permit is needed. See [tree and vegetation management](/services/tree-vegetation/).
All 13 municipalities listed on our [areas page](/areas/), from Sidney to Sooke.

faqs.q: Are you insured and registered with WorkSafeBC?
faqs.a: Liability insurance: [LIABILITY LIMIT]. WorkSafeBC: [WORKSAFEBC STATUS]. Documents are available on request.
Our workmanship guarantee: [WARRANTY]. See [how to raise a concern](/process/).

faqs.q: Are the projects and reviews on this site real?
faqs.a: Not yet. Items marked Sample are examples of the kind of work we do, not records of past jobs or words from clients. We will replace them with real projects and reviews, shared with permission.
